items.stem: Jyotsna is deciding what clothes to pack for her school trip to Mumbai in June. She looks at the weather forecast, which predicts 29°C and 84% humidity. What would be your advice to her?
items.answer:  Advise Jyotsna to pack light, breathable cotton clothes. 29°C is warm, and 84% humidity is very high, making it feel sticky and causing sweat to evaporate slowly. An umbrella or raincoat is also wise, as June is monsoon season in Mumbai.

items.stem: What is weather primarily defined as?

options.label: A
options.text: The long-term atmospheric pattern

options.label: B
options.text: The Earth’s atmospheric state presently

options.label: C
options.text: The average seasonal temperature changes

options.label: D
options.text: The study of climate variations yearly

items.answer:  (B) The Earth’s atmospheric state presently Weather refers to the state of the Earth’s atmosphere at a particular time and place. It encompasses daily or hourly conditions like temperature, humidity, and wind, which can change rapidly, unlike long-term climate patterns.

items.stem: Which layer of the Earth’s atmosphere is closest to the surface and is where most weather phenomena occur?

options.label: A
options.text: Stratosphere

options.label: B
options.text: Mesosphere

options.label: C
options.text: Troposphere

options.label: D
options.text: Thermosphere

items.answer:  (C) Troposphere The troposphere is the lowest layer of Earth’s atmosphere, extending from the ground up to about 6 to 18 kilometers. It is where all land- based life exists and nearly all weather events take place.

items.stem: Why might the troposphere be thicker in the tropical zone compared to the poles?

options.label: A
options.text: Tropical zones have more land mass

options.label: B
options.text: Polar regions experience stronger winds

options.label: C
options.text: Warmer air in tropics expands more

options.label: D
options.text: Colder air at poles contracts less

items.answer:  (C) Warmer air in tropics expands more The troposphere’s thickness varies; it is generally thicker in tropical zones because the warmer air in these regions expands, causing the atmospheric layer to extend to a greater height compared to colder polar regions where air contracts.

items.stem: Which of the following best defines “precipitation” as an element of weather?

options.label: A
options.text: The amount of water vapour in air

options.label: B
options.text: Any form of water falling from sky

options.label: C
options.text: The weight of the air above us

options.label: D
options.text: The movement of air, including speed

items.answer:  (B) Any form of water falling from sky Precipitation is any form of water, whether liquid or solid, such as rain, snow, sleet, or hail, that condenses in the atmosphere and falls to the Earth’s surface under gravity’s influence.

items.stem: What does “sleet” refer to in meteorology?

options.label: A
options.text: Small, hard balls of solid ice

options.label: B
options.text: Water in its gaseous form

options.label: C
options.text: Frozen or partly frozen falling rain

options.label: D
options.text: Light, fluffy crystals of frozen water

items.answer:  (C) Frozen or partly frozen falling rain Sleet is a form of precipitation consisting of ice pellets, which are essentially raindrops that freeze, or partially freeze, while falling through a sub-freezing layer of air near the Earth’s surface.

items.stem: Why is a commonly agreed way to measure temperature important when people from different climates communicate? perception documents

options.label: A
options.text: It helps in forecasting global weather changes

options.label: B
options.text: It prevents misunderstandings due to personal

options.label: C
options.text: It is required for international travel

options.label: D
options.text: It determines the type of clothing sold

items.answer:  (B) It prevents misunderstandings due to personal perception A standardized temperature measurement, like Celsius or Fahrenheit, allows for objective comparison. What feels “cold” in a warm climate might be “pleasant” in a colder one, so a common scale prevents subjective misinterpretations.

items.stem: Observing ants carrying their eggs to higher ground is a traditional sign indicating what upcoming weather?

options.label: A
options.text: Approaching heavy rainfall or possible floods

options.label: B
options.text: A period of prolonged dry, sunny spell

options.label: C
options.text: The onset of very strong winds

options.label: D
options.text: A sudden drop in the temperature

items.answer:  (A) Approaching heavy rainfall or possible floods Traditionally, ants moving their eggs to higher locations is interpreted as an instinctive behavior to protect their colony from impending heavy rain or potential flooding, a natural sign of weather change. Downloaded from www.pdf.tube CH 02: Understanding the Weather

items.stem: Thermometers often use a coloured liquid that _____ when the temperature increases, indicating the reading.

options.label: A
options.text: contracts

options.label: B
options.text: evaporates

options.label: C
options.text: expands

options.label: D
options.text: solidifies

items.answer:  (C) expands Many traditional thermometers contain a liquid, often mercury or colored alcohol, in a narrow tube. This liquid expands uniformly when heated and contracts when cooled, allowing temperature to be measured against a calibrated scale.

items.stem: What is the Celsius equivalent of 59 degrees Fahrenheit?

options.label: A
options.text: 10 degrees Celsius

options.label: B
options.text: 15 degrees Celsius

options.label: C
options.text: 20 degrees Celsius

options.label: D
options.text: 25 degrees Celsius

items.answer:  (B) 15 degrees Celsius The temperature scales of Celsius and Fahrenheit are interconvertible. A temperature of 15 degrees Celsius 15°C is equivalent to 59 degrees Fahrenheit (59°F), representing a cool temperature.

items.stem: What does “mean daily temperature” refer to?

options.label: A
options.text: The highest temperature recorded in a day

options.label: B
options.text: The lowest temperature recorded in a day

options.label: C
options.text: The average of maximum and minimum

options.label: D
options.text: The temperature at midday, noon

items.answer:  (C) The average of maximum and minimum The mean daily temperature is a statistical measure calculated by adding the maximum and minimum temperatures recorded during a 24- hour period and then dividing the sum by two, providing an average value.

items.stem: The India Meteorological Department (IMD) was established in which year?
items.answer:  (B) 1875 The India Meteorological Department (IMD), responsible for meteorological observations, weather forecasting, and seismology, was established in the year 1875. It plays a crucial role in monitoring and predicting weather across the country.

items.stem: The motto of the India Meteorological Department, “adityat jayate vrishti,” means “From the sun arises rain.” What scientific process does this likely refer to?

options.label: A
options.text: Solar flares causing magnetic storms

options.label: B
options.text: The sun’s heat causing water evaporation

options.label: C
options.text: Sunlight directly converting air into water

options.label: D
options.text: The sun’s gravity attracting rain clouds

items.answer:  (B) The sun’s heat causing water evaporation The sun’s energy drives the water cycle by causing evaporation from oceans, lakes, and rivers. This water vapor rises, condenses to form clouds, and eventually falls as rain, linking the sun directly to precipitation.

items.stem: If a city records a maximum temperature of 32°C and a minimum temperature of 18°C on a particular day, what is the range of temperature for that day?
items.answer:  (B) 14°C The range of temperature is the difference between the maximum and minimum temperatures recorded over a specific period. In this case, 32°C – 18°C = 14°C, which is the temperature range for the day. NODIA

items.stem: What instrument is commonly used to measure the amount of rainfall?

options.label: A
options.text: Barometer

options.label: B
options.text: Anemometer

options.label: C
options.text: Rain gauge

options.label: D
options.text: Hygrometer

items.answer:  (C) Rain gauge A rain gauge is the standard instrument used by meteorologists and weather observers to measure the amount of liquid precipitation, primarily rainfall, over a set period of time in a particular location for observation.

items.stem: When setting up a rain gauge, why should it be placed in an open area, away from objects?

options.label: A
options.text: To protect it from direct intense sunlight

options.label: B
options.text: To ensure it collects only pure rainwater

options.label: C
options.text: To prevent obstructions from blocking rain

options.label: D
options.text: To keep it safe from animals nearby

items.answer:  (C) To prevent obstructions from blocking rain A rain gauge must be placed in an open area to accurately measure rainfall. Obstructions like buildings or trees can intercept rain or cause splash-in, leading to inaccurate readings of the true amount.

items.stem: Why is atmospheric pressure generally lower at higher altitudes, like on mountains?

options.label: A
options.text: Mountains attract less air due to gravity

options.label: B
options.text: The air is denser at higher altitudes

options.label: C
options.text: There is less air above pushing down

options.label: D
options.text: Temperatures are much colder

items.answer:  (C) There is less air above pushing down At higher altitudes, there is a shorter column of air above, meaning less weight of air is pressing down. This results in lower atmospheric pressure compared to sea level or lower elevations over time.

items.stem: What is the approximate normal atmospheric pressure at sea level in millibars (mb)?

options.label: A
options.text: 650 mb

options.label: B
options.text: 900 mb

items.answer:  (C) 1013 mb The standard or normal atmospheric pressure at mean sea level is approximately 1013 millibars (mb). Pressures below 1000 mb often indicate a low-pressure system or depression, potentially leading to stormy weather conditions.

items.stem: What term is used by meteorologists when atmospheric pressure drops dramatically, potentially leading to storms?

options.label: A
options.text: An inversion

options.label: B
options.text: A heatwave

options.label: C
options.text: A depression

options.label: D
options.text: An occlusion

items.answer:  (C) A depression A dramatic drop in atmospheric pressure signifies a low-pressure system, often referred to as a depression by meteorologists. These systems can intensify and lead to unsettled weather, including storms or even cyclones in regions.

items.stem: Assertion (A) : Wind is the movement of air from areas of high pressure to areas of low pressure. Reason (R) : Differences in atmospheric pressure are primarily caused by uniform heating of the Earth’s surface. explanation of A. correct explanation of A.

options.label: A
options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct

options.label: B
options.text: Both A and R are true, but R is not the

options.label: C
options.text: A is true, but R is false

options.label: D
options.text: A is false, but R is true

items.answer:  (C) A is true, but R is false Wind is indeed the movement of air from high to low-pressure areas. However, pressure differences arise from uneven heating of the Earth’s surface, not uniform heating, which creates temperature and density variations.

items.stem: A _____ has a rotating arm with a pointer and a tail to show wind direction.

options.label: A
options.text: barometer

options.label: B
options.text: wind vane

options.label: C
options.text: hygrometer

options.label: D
options.text: thermometer

items.answer:  (B) wind vane A wind vane, also known as a weather vane, is an instrument used to indicate the direction from which the wind is blowing. It typically has a tail that causes it to orient itself with the wind.

items.stem: What is the primary purpose of a “wind sock” often seen at airports?

options.label: A
options.text: To measure the exact speed of wind

options.label: B
options.text: To indicate wind direction during take-off

options.label: C
options.text: To collect air samples for pollution

options.label: D
options.text: To generate small amounts of power

items.answer:  (B) To indicate wind direction during take-off A wind sock is a conical textile tube designed to indicate wind direction and relative wind speed. At airports, it provides pilots with a visual cue of wind conditions for safe take-offs and landings.

items.stem: What is the main difference between a wind vane and an anemometer? measures humidity measures speed measures direction measures temperature

options.label: A
options.text: Wind vane measures speed; anemometer

options.label: B
options.text: Wind vane measures direction; anemometer

options.label: C
options.text: Wind vane measures pressure; anemometer

options.label: D
options.text: Wind vane measures rainfall; anemometer

items.answer:  (B) Wind vane measures direction; anemometer measures speed A wind vane is used to determine the direction of the wind. An anemometer, on the other hand, is an instrument designed to measure the speed or velocity of the wind, often in kilometers per hour.

items.stem: What does “humidity” refer to as an element of weather?

options.label: A
options.text: The temperature of the air today

options.label: B
options.text: The pressure exerted by the air

options.label: C
options.text: The amount of water vapour in air

options.label: D
options.text: The speed of the prevailing wind

items.answer:  (C) The amount of water vapour in air Humidity is the concentration of water vapor present in the air. Water vapor, the gaseous state of water, is generally invisible to the human eye and is a key component of the atmosphere.

items.stem: Why do wet clothes typically dry faster on a day with low humidity compared to high humidity, assuming same temperature?

options.label: A
options.text: Low humidity increases air pressure aiding it

options.label: B
options.text: High humidity makes the air much heavier

options.label: C
options.text: Low humidity air can absorb more moisture

options.label: D
options.text: High humidity air contains more drying agents

items.answer:  (C) Low humidity air can absorb more moisture When humidity is low, the air has a greater capacity to absorb additional water vapor. This allows water from wet clothes to evaporate more quickly into the drier air than on a high humidity day.

items.stem: A city near the sea, like Kochi, generally experiences higher humidity than an inland desert city like Jaipur. This is primarily because the air near the sea picks up more moisture through evaporation from the large water body.

options.label: A
options.text: The sea has higher air pressure usually

options.label: B
options.text: The sea releases more pollutants in air

options.label: C
options.text: The sea is a large source of moisture

options.label: D
options.text: The sea has warmer temperatures

items.answer:  (C) The sea is a large source of moisture NODIA Coastal areas like Kochi tend to have higher humidity because of their proximity to the sea, which acts as a vast source of moisture. Evaporation from the sea surface adds water vapor to the air.

items.stem: What instrument is used to measure the humidity of the air?

options.label: A
options.text: Anemometer

options.label: B
options.text: Barometer

options.label: C
options.text: Thermometer

options.label: D
options.text: Hygrometer

items.answer:  (D) Hygrometer A hygrometer is an instrument specifically designed to measure the amount of water vapor in the air, which is known as humidity. There are various types of hygrometers based on different operating principles for this.

items.stem: What does “relative humidity” of 100% indicate?

options.label: A
options.text: The air contains absolutely no water vapour

options.label: B
options.text: The air is completely dry and arid

options.label: C
options.text: The air is saturated with water vapour

options.label: D
options.text: The air is at its coldest point

items.answer:  (C) The air is saturated with water vapour A relative humidity of 100% means the air is holding the maximum amount of water vapor it can at that particular temperature and pressure; it is saturated. Further cooling or adding more vapor would lead to condensation.

items.stem: Which of the following instrument-weather element pairings is INCORRECT?

options.label: A
options.text: Thermometer - Measures air’s temperature

options.label: B
options.text: Rain gauge - Measures total precipitation

options.label: C
options.text: Anemometer - Measures air pressure level

options.label: D
options.text: Hygrometer - Measures moisture in air

items.answer:  (C) Anemometer - Measures air pressure level An anemometer measures wind speed, not air pressure. Air pressure is measured by a barometer. Thermometers measure temperature, rain gauges measure precipitation, and hygrometers measure humidity, making the other pairs correct.

items.stem: What is the primary function of an Automated Weather Station (AWS)?

options.label: A
options.text: To manually record observations by staff

options.label: B
options.text: To provide long-range climate change models

options.label: C
options.text: To automatically measure and record weather

options.label: D
options.text: To control local weather conditions artificially

items.answer:  (C) To automatically measure and record weather An Automated Weather Station (AWS) is designed to automatically measure and record various weather parameters like temperature, humidity, wind, and precipitation using sensors, without needing human intervention for routine data collection.

items.stem: Why is it particularly important for farmers to be aware of wind data like speed and direction?

options.label: A
options.text: Wind affects the visibility for planting crops

options.label: B
options.text: Wind influences soil dryness and rain patterns

options.label: C
options.text: Strong winds can damage farm equipment

options.label: D
options.text: Wind helps in pollinating all crop types

items.answer:  (B) Wind influences soil dryness and rain patterns Wind speed affects how quickly soil dries out, and wind direction can help predict where rain might come from. Both are crucial for farmers in planning irrigation, planting, and other agricultural activities effectively.

items.stem: Meteorologists collect weather data over long periods. What is the primary purpose of this long- term data collection?

options.label: A
options.text: To write historical accounts of weather events

options.label: B
options.text: To study the impact of weather on monuments

options.label: C
options.text: To predict future weather and climate patterns

options.label: D
options.text: To determine the best locations for cities

items.answer:  (C) To predict future weather and climate patterns Long-term weather data allows meteorologists to identify patterns, understand climatic trends, and develop more accurate models for forecasting future weather conditions and studying climate change, which is crucial for planning.

items.stem: How do weather predictions, such as those for heavy rain or cyclones, help local governments? weather taxes fast industry Downloaded from www.pdf.tube CH 02: Understanding the Weather

options.label: A
options.text: They allow governments to change the

options.label: B
options.text: They enable governments to collect more

options.label: C
options.text: They help governments to mobilize resources

options.label: D
options.text: They primarily boost the local tourism

items.answer:  (C) They help governments to mobilize resources fast Accurate weather predictions enable local governments to prepare for potential disasters by mobilizing resources, alerting communities, and planning evacuation or relief efforts, thereby minimizing damage and ensuring public safety from all.

items.stem: What is the unit generally used to display atmospheric pressure on a barometer?

options.label: A
options.text: Celsius

options.label: B
options.text: Millimeter

options.label: C
options.text: Millibar

options.label: D
options.text: Kilometer

items.answer:  (C) Millibar Barometers, instruments used to measure atmospheric pressure, typically display readings in millibars (mb). This unit is a standard in meteorology for reporting and comparing atmospheric pressure values across different locations and times.

items.stem: Pine cones are known to _____ in humid conditions to protect their seeds.

options.label: A
options.text: open

options.label: B
options.text: close

options.label: C
options.text: shrink

options.label: D
options.text: expand

items.answer:  (B) close Pine cones exhibit a natural mechanism where they close their scales in humid or wet conditions. This action helps to protect the seeds within from unfavorable moisture levels until drier conditions prevail for dispersal.

items.stem: What is meant by “water vapour”?

options.label: A
options.text: Tiny droplets of liquid water suspended

options.label: B
options.text: Water in its solid, icy crystal form

options.label: C
options.text: Water in its gaseous, invisible state

options.label: D
options.text: A mixture of water and air pollutants

items.answer:  (C) Water in its gaseous, invisible state Water vapour is the term for water when it is in its gaseous state, as opposed to liquid water NODIA or solid ice. It is an important component of the atmosphere and plays a key role in weather.

items.stem: Which of these is NOT listed as one of the five main elements of weather?

options.label: A
options.text: Temperature condition

options.label: B
options.text: Cloud cover

options.label: C
options.text: Wind movements

options.label: D
options.text: Humidity level

items.answer:  (B) Cloud cover The five main elements of weather typically discussed are temperature, precipitation, atmospheric pressure, wind (speed and direction), and humidity. While cloud cover is related to weather, it’s often considered a characteristic resulting from these primary elements.

items.stem: Why is it important for meteorologists to measure both the speed and direction of wind? only

options.label: A
options.text: It helps determine the exact temperature

options.label: B
options.text: It indicates the likelihood of earthquakes soon

options.label: C
options.text: It influences air travel and sailing significantly

options.label: D
options.text: It directly causes changes in air pressure

items.answer:  (C) It influences air travel and sailing significantly Wind speed and direction are crucial for various applications, including aviation and sailing, as they directly impact flight paths and sea navigation. They also help in forecasting weather patterns, such as the movement of storms.

items.stem: Which of the following pairs correctly matches a traditional weather predictor with the weather it typically indicates?

options.label: A
options.text: Birds flying high - Approaching heavy storm

options.label: B
options.text: Frogs croaking loudly - Prolonged dry spell

options.label: C
options.text: Pine cones opening - High humidity level

options.label: D
options.text: Ants moving eggs high - Coming rain

items.answer:  (D) Ants moving eggs high - Coming rain Many traditional weatherlores exist. Ants moving their eggs to higher ground is often seen as an indicator of impending rain. Birds flying low (not high) might suggest storms, and pine cones close in high humidity.

items.stem: The National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA) set up an Automated Weather Station (AWS) in 2023 at a glacial lake in which Indian state?

options.label: A
options.text: Uttarakhand

options.label: B
options.text: Himachal Pradesh

options.label: C
options.text: Sikkim

options.label: D
options.text: Arunachal Pradesh

items.answer:  (C) Sikkim In 2023, the NDMA installed an AWS at a high- altitude glacial lake in Sikkim. This station provides crucial early information about weather conditions, which is vital for disaster preparedness in such sensitive regions.

items.stem: If the relative humidity in Jaipur is 30% and in Mumbai it is 75% on the same day with similar temperatures, where would you expect to sweat more and feel “stickier”? evaporation

options.label: A
options.text: Jaipur, because dry air absorbs sweat quickly

options.label: B
options.text: Mumbai, because high humidity slows sweat

options.label: C
options.text: Equally in both, as temperature is similar

options.label: D
options.text: Neither, as sweating depends on wind speed

items.answer:  (B) Mumbai, because high humidity slows sweat evaporation High relative humidity, as in Mumbai (75%), means the air is already quite moist. This slows down the evaporation of sweat from the skin, making one feel hotter and “stickier” than in drier air.

options.label: C

items.answer:  (A) Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A. Digital thermometers offer advantages like higher precision and the ability to store data, making them more suitable for detailed meteorological records and analysis compared to traditional liquid-in-glass types which are older.

items.stem: Which of the following weather phenomena and its primary characteristic is an INCORRECT pairing? hotness winds

options.label: A
options.text: Heat Wave - Prolonged period of excessive

options.label: B
options.text: Cold Wave - Rapid and significant drop

options.label: C
options.text: Ground Frost - Ice formation on ground surface

options.label: D
options.text: Dust Storm - Heavy rainfall with strong

items.answer:  (D) Dust Storm - Heavy rainfall with strong winds A dust storm is characterized by strong winds carrying large quantities of dust over an extensive area, typically in arid or semi-arid regions. Heavy rainfall is not a defining feature; in fact, they often occur in dry conditions.

items.stem: Wind speed is measured in kilometers per hour. Which of the above statements is/are correct?

options.label: A
options.text: 1 and 2 only

options.label: B
options.text: 3 only

options.label: C
options.text: 2 and 3 only

options.label: D
options.text: 1, 2 and 3

items.answer:  (B) 3 only Atmospheric pressure decreases with altitude. Humidity is the amount of water vapor in the air, not its weight (which relates to pressure). Wind speed is commonly measured in units like kilometers per hour (km/h).

items.stem: The layer of gases that surrounds planets like Earth is called the _____.

options.label: A
options.text: lithosphere

options.label: B
options.text: hydrosphere

options.label: C
options.text: atmosphere

options.label: D
options.text: biosphere

items.answer:  (C) atmosphere The atmosphere is the envelope of gases surrounding a planet or other celestial body. Earth’s atmosphere is composed mainly of nitrogen and oxygen and is essential for life and weather processes.

items.stem: Why is it that “what is cold for Krishnan (from Chennai) may be pleasant for Amir (from Kashmir)”? clothes climates

options.label: A
options.text: People from different regions have different

options.label: B
options.text: Their bodies are physiologically adapted to

options.label: C
options.text: They use different types of heating systems

options.label: D
options.text: They speak different languages about weather

items.answer:  (B) Their bodies are physiologically adapted to climates People adapt to the typical climate of their region. What someone from a consistently warm place like Chennai perceives as cold might be considered mild or pleasant by someone accustomed to colder conditions like in Kashmir.

items.stem: The opening and closing of pine cones are natural mechanisms driven by what environmental factor?

options.label: A
options.text: Changes in ambient light intensity

options.label: B
options.text: Fluctuations in atmospheric air pressure

options.label: C
options.text: Variations in environmental wind speed

options.label: D
options.text: Changes in environmental humidity levels

items.answer:  (D) Changes in environmental humidity levels Pine cones open and close in response to changes in environmental humidity. They tend to close up in damp or humid conditions to protect seeds and open up in dry conditions to release them.

items.stem: What does the term “forecast” mean in the context of weather?

options.label: A
options.text: To document past weather events accurately

options.label: B
options.text: To predict or find out in advance

options.label: C
options.text: To measure current atmospheric conditions

options.label: D
options.text: To study the causes of weather change

items.answer:  (B) To predict or find out in advance Downloaded from www.pdf.tube In meteorology, a forecast is a prediction of future weather conditions for a specific location and time period. It is based on analysis of current conditions and meteorological models of all data.

items.stem: How does the process of evaporation cause a cooling effect on a surface? surface

options.label: A
options.text: Evaporation adds heat to the nearby air

options.label: B
options.text: Evaporation consumes heat energy from

options.label: C
options.text: Evaporation releases cold particles into air

options.label: D
options.text: Evaporation reduces the air pressure above

items.answer:  (B) Evaporation consumes heat energy from surface Evaporation is a cooling process because the phase change from liquid to gas requires energy (latent heat of vaporization). This energy is absorbed from the surface where evaporation occurs, thus lowering its temperature.

items.stem: In which temperature scale is the freezing point of water 0°C and the boiling point 100°C?

options.label: A
options.text: Fahrenheit scale

options.label: B
options.text: Celsius scale

options.label: C
options.text: Kelvin scale

options.label: D
options.text: Rankine scale

items.answer:  (B) Celsius scale The Celsius scale is defined by setting the freezing point of water at 0°C and the boiling point of water at 100°C at standard atmospheric pressure. It is widely used globally for temperature measurement.

items.stem: Explain briefly why we experience weather only in the troposphere.
items.answer:  The troposphere is the lowest layer of the atmosphere where almost all water vapour and atmospheric activity (clouds, storms) occur, and it’s where we live. NODIA CH 02: Understanding the Weather

items.stem: How does the thickness of the troposphere vary between the poles and the tropics?
items.answer:  The troposphere is thicker in the warmer tropical zone because warm air expands, and less thick at the colder poles where cold air contracts.

items.stem: Why is it necessary to have standard ways to measure weather elements like temperature?
items.answer:  Standard measurements allow people in different places (like Krishnan in Chennai and Amir in Kashmir) to accurately communicate and compare weather conditions, avoiding confusion based on personal feeling.

items.stem: Give two examples of how animals’ behaviour can traditionally indicate weather changes.
items.answer:  Ants carrying their eggs to higher ground can indicate expected heavy rain. Frogs croaking loudly are often believed to signal the arrival of rain.

items.stem: How do pine cones help indicate humidity levels?
items.answer:  Pine cones naturally close their scales in humid conditions to protect seeds and open them in dry conditions to release seeds, acting as natural humidity indicators.

items.stem: What is the difference between a clinical thermometer and a laboratory thermometer?
items.answer:  Clinical thermometers are used for measuring body temperature with a specific range, while laboratory thermometers measure a wider range of temperatures found in experiments or the environment.

items.stem: How is the ‘range of temperature’ for a day calculated?
items.answer:  The range of temperature is calculated by subtracting the minimum temperature recorded during a specific period (usually 24 hours) from the maximum temperature recorded during that same period.

items.stem: Explain the principle behind how a rain gauge measures rainfall.
items.answer:  A rain gauge uses a funnel to collect rainwater into a calibrated measuring cylinder. The depth of the collected water directly indicates the amount of rainfall received over an area.

items.stem: Why does atmospheric pressure decrease as we go higher up a mountain?
items.answer:  As altitude increases, the column of air above gets shorter and thinner, meaning there is less air pressing down, resulting in lower atmospheric pressure.

items.stem: Why might people feel breathless or dizzy at high altitudes?
items.answer:  At high altitudes, lower atmospheric pressure means the air is thinner with less oxygen. The body gets less oxygen, making it work harder, causing breathlessness or dizziness.

items.stem: What is a ‘depression’ in meteorological terms?
items.answer:  A depression is a low-pressure system where atmospheric pressure drops significantly below the normal level (e.g., below 1000 mb), often leading to stormy weather or cyclones.

items.stem: Why is measuring atmospheric pressure important for weather forecasting?
items.answer:  Monitoring changes in atmospheric pressure, especially sudden drops, helps meteorologists predict the formation and movement of storms, depressions, or cyclones, enabling timely warnings.

items.stem: Explain the function of a wind vane (weather vane).
items.answer:  A wind vane has a pointer and a tail that rotates freely. The wind pushes the tail, causing the pointer to align with and indicate the direction from which the wind is blowing. NODIA

items.stem: How does an anemometer measure wind speed?
items.answer:  An anemometer has cups that rotate when the wind blows. A meter counts the rotations over time and calculates the wind speed, typically in kilometres per hour (km/h).

items.stem: Why would humidity likely be higher in Kochi than in Jaipur?
items.answer:  Kochi is a coastal city, close to the sea which is a large source of water vapour through evaporation, leading to higher humidity compared to Jaipur, which is inland.

items.stem: How does humidity affect the rate at which water evaporates?
items.answer:  When humidity is high (more water vapour already in the air), the rate of evaporation slows down because the air cannot easily absorb more moisture.

items.stem: Explain why wet clothes dry faster in Delhi (52% humidity) than in Kochi (84% humidity), assuming the same temperature.
items.answer:  Delhi’s air has lower relative humidity (52%), meaning it can absorb more moisture. Therefore, water evaporates faster from wet clothes in Delhi compared to Kochi’s more saturated air (84% humidity).

items.stem: Give one reason why measuring humidity is important in industries or museums.
items.answer:  Museums monitor humidity to maintain a dry environment, preventing damage to delicate exhibits. Food processing industries control humidity for product quality and preservation.

items.stem: What is the main advantage of an Automated Weather Station (AWS)?
items.answer:  An AWS operates automatically using sensors to measure and record weather data continuously without needing human intervention, providing timely and accurate information.

items.stem: How do meteorologists use the data collected from weather instruments?
items.answer:  Meteorologists study long-term data collected from various instruments, analyse patterns, and use scientific methods and models to predict future weather conditions.

items.stem: Why have accurate weather predictions become more important recently?
items.answer:  Due to climate change, extreme weather events like droughts, floods, and cyclones are becoming more frequent, making accurate predictions crucial for preparedness and safety.

items.stem: Give an example of how a weather warning helps people stay safe.
items.answer:  If a cyclone is predicted, warnings allow authorities to evacuate coastal areas, or fishermen can be warned not to go out to sea, preventing loss of life and property.

items.stem: How is weather different from climate ?
items.answer:  Weather describes the atmospheric conditions at a specific time and place, while climate (to be discussed later) refers to the average weather patterns over a long period. LONG ANSWER QUESTIO 

items.stem: Analyse the statement : “Weather is the state of the Earth’s atmosphere at a particular time and place.” Why are ‘time’ and ‘place’ crucial?
items.answer:  Weather constantly changes. Temperature, wind, or rain can differ significantly from morning to evening (time) or between a coastal city and an inland town (place) on the same day. Therefore, specifying both time and place is essential for an accurate description of the weather conditions.

items.stem: Explain the relationship between temperature and the state of coconut oil or setting curd.
items.answer:  Coconut oil solidifies in cold winter temperatures because its freezing point is relatively high. Curd sets slower in cold weather because the bacteria responsible for fermentation work more slowly at lower temperatures. Both illustrate how temperature affects physical or biological processes.

items.stem: Analyse the significance of the IMD’s motto, “From the sun arises rain,” connecting it to the water cycle.
items.answer:  The sun’s energy drives the water cycle. It causes water from oceans, lakes, and rivers to evaporate (turn into water vapour). This vapour rises, cools, condenses into clouds, and eventually falls as precipitation (rain). Thus, the sun is the primary energy source initiating the process that leads to rain.

items.stem: Compare the challenges faced by people living at sea level versus those living at very high altitudes like Khardung La, concerning atmospheric pressure.
items.answer:  At sea level, atmospheric pressure is high, and oxygen is abundant, making breathing easy. At Khardung La (high altitude), pressure is significantly lower, air is thinner, and oxygen is scarce. This forces the body to work harder, potentially causing breathlessness, fatigue, and requiring acclimatisation for survival.

items.stem: Analyse how understanding wind direction and speed is crucial for different professions like pilots, sailors, and farmers.
items.answer:  Pilots and sailors need wind data for navigation, safety, and fuel efficiency, as wind affects aircraft/ ship speed and direction. Farmers use wind NODIA direction to predict rain movement and wind speed to gauge soil drying rates, aiding decisions about planting or irrigation.

items.stem: Explain the process of evaporation and its relationship with humidity and drying clothes.
items.answer:  Evaporation is water turning into vapour, causing cooling. High humidity means the air already holds much vapour, slowing evaporation. Low humidity allows faster evaporation. Therefore, clothes dry quicker in low humidity air (which can absorb more moisture) than in high humidity air (which is already nearly saturated).

items.stem: Analyse the importance of Automated Weather Stations (AWS) in remote or harsh environments like glacial lakes in Sikkim.
items.answer:  AWS are vital in remote/harsh locations because they operate automatically, eliminating the need for risky human presence. They provide continuous, crucial data (temperature, pressure, precipitation) from inaccessible areas like high-altitude glacial lakes, enabling early warnings for potential hazards like floods caused by lake outbursts.

items.stem: Evaluate the role of weather forecasting in disaster management, using examples like cyclones or heat waves.
items.answer:  Forecasting is critical for disaster management. Predicting a cyclone allows timely evacuations of coastal areas and warnings to fishermen. Forecasting heat waves enables authorities to issue health advisories, open cooling centres, and manage resources like power and water, significantly reducing risks to life and property.

items.stem: Why might traditional weather prediction methods (observing nature) still be relevant today, alongside scientific meteorology?
items.answer:  Traditional methods, based on generations of local observation, can offer immediate, hyperlocal insights complementing broader scientific forecasts. Animal behaviour or plant changes might signal subtle shifts specific to a micro-environment that large-scale models miss, providing valuable context for local communities, especially farmers or fishermen.

items.stem: Analyse the connection between atmospheric pressure changes and the formation of wind.
items.answer:  The atmosphere seeks equilibrium. When heating/cooling creates areas of differing air pressure (weight), air naturally flows from the region of higher pressure towards the region of lower pressure to balance it out. This horizontal movement of air is what we experience as wind.

items.stem: Explain why knowing both wind speed and direction is important for understanding its impact.
items.answer:  Wind direction tells us where the air (and potentially weather like rain clouds or pollution) is coming from or going towards. Wind speed tells us the force of the wind, determining its potential impact – from gentle seed dispersal to causing soil erosion or posing dangers for flights/sailing.

items.stem: Analyse how the development of precise weather instruments has advanced the science of meteorology.
items.answer:  Precise instruments allow objective, quantifiable measurement of weather elements (temperature, pressure, humidity, etc.), replacing subjective observation. This provides accurate, standardized data essential for identifying patterns, developing scientific models, testing hypotheses, and making increasingly reliable weather forecasts, thus advancing meteorology significantly.

items.stem: Evaluate the statement : “Understanding weather helps us adapt our daily lives.”
items.answer:  This is true. We adapt by choosing clothes based on temperature (warm clothes in winter, cool in summer). We plan activities based on forecasts (e.g., packing rain gear if rain is predicted). Understanding humidity helps predict how quickly clothes will dry or how comfortable we might feel outdoors. items.stem: A farmer in North India wants to spray pesticides on his crops. The weather forecast predicts calm conditions in the morning but strong ‘Loo’ winds developing in the afternoon, with temperatures reaching 42°C. He needs to decide the best time to spray to ensure effectiveness and safety. (i) What weather element poses the biggest challenge for spraying in the afternoon? (ii) Explain why spraying during strong winds is not advisable. (iii) Based on the forecast, when should the farmer ideally spray the pesticides? Justify your answer.
items.answer:  (i) The strong ‘Loo’ winds pose the biggest challenge. (ii) Strong winds can cause the pesticide spray to drift away from the target crops, reducing effectiveness and potentially harming nearby areas or people. (iii) The farmer should spray in the morning when conditions are predicted to be calm. This ensures the spray settles on the crops effectively before the strong afternoon winds start.

items.stem: Mountaineers preparing to climb a high peak in the Himalayas check the weather report. It shows rapidly falling atmospheric pressure (dropped by 15 mb in 12 hours) and increasing wind speeds, although the sky is currently clear. (i) What weather event might the falling pressure and increasing winds indicate? (ii) Why should the mountaineers be concerned even if the sky is currently clear? (iii) What safety precaution should the mountaineers consider based on this forecast?
items.answer:  (i) Rapidly falling pressure indicates an approaching low-pressure system or depression, which often brings stormy weather and strong winds. (ii) Weather conditions, especially in mountains, can change rapidly. Falling pressure is a strong indicator of deteriorating weather, meaning storms could develop quickly despite current clear skies. (iii) They should consider postponing their ascent or seeking shelter at a lower altitude until the weather system passes and conditions stabilize, as climbing during a storm is extremely dangerous.

items.stem: A museum curator in Chennai notices that some old paintings are showing signs of mould. The museum’s internal reading shows a consistent relative humidity of 75% and a temperature of 28°C. An expert suggests controlling the humidity. (i) Is 75% relative humidity considered high or low. (ii) What instrument would the museum use to measure this humidity level? (iii) Explain why controlling humidity is crucial for preserving museum exhibits like paintings.
items.answer:  (i) 75% relative humidity falls within the humid range (60%-80%), so it is considered high. (ii) The museum would use a hygrometer to measure relative humidity. (iii) High humidity promotes the growth of mould and mildew, which can damage sensitive materials like canvas and paint. Maintaining lower, stable humidity helps prevent such biological deterioration and preserves the artifacts.

items.stem: During the monsoon season, a weather station in Cherrapunji records 150 mm of rainfall in a single day. A nearby station in Shillong records only 20 mm on the same day. Both use standard rain gauges. (i) What instrument is used to get these readings? (ii) What does ‘150 mm of rainfall’ mean in practical terms? (iii) Evaluate what this data suggests about rainfall patterns, even over relatively short distances.
items.answer:  (i) A rain gauge is used to measure rainfall. (ii) It means that if the rain that fell over an area was collected without any runoff or evaporation, it would form a layer of water 150 mm (or 15 cm) deep. (iii) This suggests that rainfall, especially during monsoon, can be highly variable locally. Geographic factors like hills or wind patterns can cause one place (Cherrapunji) to receive extremely heavy rain while a nearby area (Shillong) receives much less. NODIA

items.stem: An airplane is scheduled to fly from Jaipur (relatively dry) to Kochi (humid). The pilot checks the weather reports, including temperature, wind speed/direction, and atmospheric pressure for both locations and the route. (i) Why is atmospheric pressure information important for aviation? (ii) How might the difference in humidity between Jaipur and Kochi affect the flight or passenger comfort? (iii) Besides pressure and humidity, why is wind data crucial for the pilot?
items.answer:  (i) Atmospheric pressure affects aircraft performance (lift, engine power) and altimeter settings. Pilots need accurate pressure data for safe altitude calculations and flight planning. (ii) While cabin air is conditioned, high humidity in Kochi might affect ground operations or passenger comfort upon arrival. Very low humidity in Jaipur might affect engine performance slightly differently during takeoff compared to Kochi. (iii) Wind speed and direction significantly impact flight time, fuel consumption, and takeoff/ landing safety.
